title: Two weeks after releasing my first game, I finally got the FULL game working in the browser! 😅
author: Every-Leave7093
selftext:
[Click here to play in browser! ](https://dfenech1982.itch.io/1565-the-great-siege)

About two weeks ago, I released my first game, 1565 - The Great Siege, as a download for Windows, Mac and Linux.

One thing I quickly learned is that people want the least amount of effort possible to try a game... so having a browser version seemed like the obvious answer! 😂

The problem was that my previous WebGL version couldn't save progress between sessions, so I could only release a short demo.

With the help of AI (and a few pointers from a fellow Redditor), I finally managed to get persistent saves working!

You can now play the FULL game directly in your browser, save your progress and come back later to continue where you left off! 🎉

In the meantime, I also made a new gameplay-focused trailer, which I hope gives a better feel for what 1565 is actually like.

Next on my list is making the game mobile-friendly!

To be honest, with the resolution I used for the game (320×180), it actually looks really nice on a mobile screen. But there's one problem...

The game uses left click to interact with things and right click to look at them.

I'm thinking of making a normal finger tap equal a left click, while holding your finger down for about 0.5 seconds would act as a right click.

Has anyone here done something similar with Unity WebGL? How did you go about it? I'd love to hear your suggestions!

And thanks again to this community for all the support you've given my game! ❤️

comments.author: geoffsykes
comments.body: Dude, seriously, this looks fantastic. Excellent work.
